clue.text: Accessories to assault at golf course

parts.note: to cuff someone is to strike them, an assault
links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: Someone is charged with attacking a fellow player out on the fairways.
explanation.definitionFit: Cufflinks are fasteners worn at the shirt cuff, a gentleman's accessories.

clue.text: Fish taking care of weed

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
to hoe is to weed with a garden tool

explanation.surface: A gardener tends to the weeding while minding the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The cohoe, or coho, is a Pacific salmon.

clue.text: Sought food intended to be given to the elderly

parts.note: a present for someone is meant to be given to them
the aged are the elderly

explanation.surface: Someone went hunting for meals meant for old people.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search for food, so foraged means sought it.

clue.text: One collecting charge gives Dutch city shock

parts.note: Leyden is an old spelling of Leiden in the Netherlands
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A tax collector gets a jolt in a town in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee but is electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leyden jar is an early capacitor, a glass vessel that stores electric charge.

clue.text: Behind punt, I struggled to stop early on

indicators.note: struggled suggests letters thrashing about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rower behind a punt fights to halt at the start of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggled' rearranges BEHIND, PUNT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip something in the bud is an idiom for stopping it at an early stage.

clue.text: Put into words what 27's early stages convey

definitions.meaning: the opening letters of 27 across are E and G, the abbreviation for for example

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: E.G. stands for 'for example', another meaning of say.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to express it in words, and say also means for example.

clue.text: Method of dyeing Christopher and Jack have backed

indicators.note: backed tells us the two names together are read from right to left

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: Two men named Christopher and Jack have put money on a way of colouring cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have backed' turns KITAB round to give the answer. Jack and AB are both crossword sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a wax-resist technique for patterning fabric with dye.

clue.text: Country cottage's telephone line taken out

indicators.note: taken out means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A rural cottage has had its phone line removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Blower is old British slang for the phone; the 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a poetic word for a cottage or rustic dwelling, as well as a leafy shelter.

clue.text: City aware of rubbish piled up higher

indicators.note: higher places the first piece above the second in the column
in a down clue, piled up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
to be on to someone is to be aware of what they are up to

explanation.surface: A city knows its rubbish heaps are growing ever taller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' turns ROT into TOR, set 'higher' than ONTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: 17 castles a king's put on boundaries of estates

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above the following piece

parts.note: keeps are the strongholds of castles, standing for castles
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: boundaries are the outside edges, so the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fortified homes and a monarch sit on the edges of country estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is MEMORABILIA, souvenirs. 'boundaries of' gives ES, the first and last letters of estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepsakes are objects kept in memory of someone, the same as memorabilia.

clue.text: You've little time to go round city in America — yes, get a move on

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time is made to surround the ancient city

parts.note: HR is the short form of hour, a little time
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
yup is the American informal way of saying yes

explanation.surface: A traveller is told there is barely time to do a tour of a US city before moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You've' only sets the scene. Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the crossword's favourite city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic urgings to someone to move faster.

clue.text: One gave us bows, yet we're put out

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thanked for a performance is nonetheless annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges YET WE'RE. Medieval longbows were made of yew wood, which is why the definition works.
explanation.definitionFit: Yew timber was the classic material for English longbows, so the tree literally supplied bows.

clue.text: Standard, or two strokes fewer?

definitions.meaning: the standard carried by a Roman legion
in golf, finishing a hole two shots under par

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are joined by 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion's emblem was an eagle on a pole, and a golfer scoring two under par makes an eagle.

clue.text: Numbers in sequence? On the contrary, without any conditions

indicators.note: in would put the first piece inside the second, but the next words reverse that
on the contrary says the containment runs the other way, sequence inside numbers

parts.note: a string is a sequence of items, as in a string of wins

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether figures are in order and receives an unconditional reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'in' would put the numbers inside the sequence; 'On the contrary' swaps which piece goes inside which.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal with no strings attached carries no conditions; the idiom means unconditional.

clue.text: Choir splash out, providing financial aid

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choir spends lavishly on a fund that supports students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CHOIR and SPLASH; 'providing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarship is a grant of money to support a student's education.

clue.text: Fish to be paid for when it arrives

definitions.text: to be paid for when it arrives

explanation.definitionFit: Cod is a sea fish, and goods sent cash on delivery are paid for on arrival.

clue.text: City turned up, we hear, to game

indicators.note: we hear means the first piece is given by its pronunciation

parts.note: came means turned up or arrived
bridge is the card game

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a town, by report, for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes CAME sound like the first syllable of the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city.

clue.text: Signature of American comedian (omitting the Anthony)

indicators.note: omitting means the given first name is dropped from the full name

parts.note: the British comedian Tony Hancock was born Anthony John Hancock
the first forename of that comedian, taken out

explanation.surface: A request for a famous American comic's autograph, minus one of his names.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Hancock was a much-loved British radio and TV comedian of the 1950s and 60s. John Hancock's large signature on the US Declaration of Independence made his name American slang for a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a person's signature is jokingly called their John Hancock, after the bold Declaration signatory.

clue.text: Worthless coconut — an anomaly

indicators.note: an anomaly is an irregularity, so these letters are out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coconut that is a freak of nature is considered valueless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anomaly' rearranges COCONUT and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no account is of no importance or value.

clue.text: Souvenirs of Liberia — ammo that's been shot

indicators.note: something shot is blasted apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keepsakes from a West African war zone include spent cartridges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been shot' rearranges LIBERIA and AMMO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorabilia are objects kept as souvenirs of people or events.

clue.text: Parody makes tragic heroine weep

parts.note: Mimi is the dying heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
to cry is to weep

explanation.surface: A send-up has the opera's doomed heroine sobbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is imitation, often to make fun of someone, as in parody.

clue.text: Mothers admitted regularly in embassy

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word, starting from the second, admits only some of its letters

explanation.surface: Mums are let into an embassy at set intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted regularly in' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of EMBASSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma is an informal word for mother; the plural gives mothers.

clue.text: Planet Henry put in order

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A man named Henry arranges the planets.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal is to arrange people or things in order.

clue.text: Prompt answer received, supplying balance

indicators.note: received tells us one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: a prompt is a reminder

explanation.surface: A quick reply arrives, settling what is still owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning quick but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the balance outstanding.

clue.text: The thirteenth or fifteenth time, in other words

parts.note: in the Roman calendar the ides fell on the 13th or 15th of the month

explanation.surface: A diarist notes a certain day of the month, rephrasing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ides was the 15th of March, May, July and October, and the 13th of other months.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est, Latin for 'that is', introduces a rephrasing, the same as in other words.

clue.text: Girl seen to sing happily

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are joined by 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a girl's name, and as a verb it means to sing joyfully, like a bird.

clue.text: Pull-in set aside for future needs

definitions.meaning: a pull-in is a roadside stopping place

explanation.definitionFit: A lay-by is a British roadside parking spot, and to lay by is to put aside for later.

clue.text: The devil knows policemen are about early on

indicators.note: early on puts the turned piece at the front
are about means the letters for the police are turned round

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes police
ken means know, so kens is knows

explanation.surface: Satan is aware that officers are nearby from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are about' turns the police letters round, and 'early on' puts them first. 'What the dickens' is a mild oath meaning the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens is an old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the dickens?'.

clue.text: Dry in a very short space of time

definitions.text: a very short space of time

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are joined by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec is French for dry, used of wine, and also short for a second of time.

clue.text: Henry, with anything at all unknown, is contemptuous

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
aught is an old word meaning anything whatever
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A man named Henry, knowing nothing about anything, looks down on others.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'is contemptuous' standing in for an adjective after 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haughty person is arrogant and disdainful, looking down on others.

clue.text: Covering up swindle in France and another country

indicators.note: covering up means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: et is French for and
a gyp is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A fraud in France is hushed up and spreads to another nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to France as the first country mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country of North Africa, a different one from France.

clue.text: Admirably, EU policy line accepted by member country

parts.note: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union

indicators.note: accepted by means a piece is taken inside the following one

parts.note: Italy is a member country of the EU

explanation.surface: An EU farming rule is well received by one of the member states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts L inside ITALY.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitally is a dated British way of saying excellently or admirably.
